title: Capitalist China, Socialist America?
author: Edmund Wilson
content:
![Capitalist China, Socialist
America?](https://storage.ghost.io/c/65/af/65afbdb5-30bf-4286-acc4-9535069adb42/content/images/2026/08/Screenshot-2026-08-31-at-7.28.45
---AM.png)

In recent years, heightened tensions between the United States and China have
led to talk of a new Cold War. The standard framing of this conflict, both
from the anti-imperialist left and the civilizationist right, reprises themes
of the twentieth century, treating it as a struggle between colonizer and
colonized or capitalism and communism.

The 2020 book  _Trade Wars Are Class Wars_ , by the economists Matthew Klein
and Michael Pettis, complicates this view. Klein and Pettis, whose ideas have
influenced both Biden and Trump officials, drew on J.A. Hobson's classic
theory of imperialism, which argued that Britain had dumped goods on colonies
and flushed out excess savings abroad through mobile finance capital.

Today, Klein and Pettis argue, the relationship between imperial metropole and
colonial periphery is reversed. The supposed inheritor of the British imperial
legacy, the United States, sells its financial assets overseas while [
_buying_](https://phenomenalworld.org/analysis/trade-and-the-manufacturing-
share/?ref=compactmag.com) the surplus production of creditor countries such
as China. America is indebted to China and buys Chinese products as well as
products manufactured in countries indebted to China through the Belt and Road
Initiative.
